title: Many-Anyon Braiding in Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall Effect with Hybrid Monte Carlo Simulation
authors: Ting-Tung Wang, Ha Quang Trung, Qianhui Xu, Min Long, Bo Yang, Zi Yang Meng
abstract: We employ the hybrid Monte Carlo method to efficiently compute the many-anyon non-Abelian braiding matrices associated with different braiding schemes of the Moore-Read quasiholes. A novel proposal in this work is that anyon braiding schemes based on a global rotation are robust against finite-size effects, as demonstrated by benchmarking their errors in the braiding matrix against those of a simple two-anyon exchange. Moreover, we investigate how electron-electron interactions and local electrostatic trapping potentials influence the energetic preference of different fusion channels. Their effect on the non-Abelian braiding matrices has been verified, a surprising phenomenon that demonstrates long-range entanglement of non-Abelian states. Our results are relevant to the experimental realization of non-Abelian physics in fractional quantum Hall and other analogous systems, including the fast-growing field of fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moiré materials.
summary: This work uses advanced numerical simulations to study non-Abelian braiding in the Fractional Quantum Hall Effect using the Moore-Read model. By comparing different braiding paths and incorporating external potentials, the authors show that rotational braiding is robust against finite-size errors. Crucially, they demonstrate that the braiding statistics can be actively controlled by tuning the balance between electron-electron interactions and local trapping fields.
main_problem: To compute and analyze the many-anyon non-Abelian braiding matrices associated with different braiding schemes of Moore-Read quasiholes, accounting for finite-size effects and external interactions.
main_result: The rotational braiding scheme is shown to be significantly more robust against finite-size effects than classical braiding, and the braiding statistics can be controlled by tuning the competition between electron-electron interactions and local trapping potentials.
method: The Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) method is employed to efficiently compute the braiding matrices by projecting the Hamiltonian onto the quasihole manifold and analyzing the adiabatic evolution operator.
model_or_system: The study models the Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall Effect using the Moore-Read (MR) state for quasiholes. The Hamiltonian includes terms for the MR state, Coulomb interaction, and local electrostatic trapping potentials.
key_observables: Non-Abelian braiding matrices, the relative eigenvalue phase ($\alpha = \lambda_1 / \lambda_2$), and the statistical Berry phase ($\gamma_{	ext{stat}}$).
important_parameters: The strength of the local pinning potential ($h$), the number of quasiholes ($2n=4, 6$), and the separation distance of the anyons.
main_assumptions: The model wavefunctions are not exact eigenstates of realistic Hamiltonians, and the analysis relies on the assumption that the system remains adiabatically connected to the model Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures compare the finite-size dependence of the relative eigenvalue phase ($\alpha$) for classical versus rotational braiding schemes, showing the superior convergence of the rotational scheme. Other figures illustrate how the fusion channel selection dictates the braiding statistics.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares different braiding protocols (classical vs. rotational) and investigates the influence of external potentials (trapping) on the resulting braiding matrices. It details the mathematical framework using the evolution operator and the key observable $\alpha$.
why_interesting: The demonstration of how external potentials can tune the fusion channel, thereby controlling the non-Abelian braiding statistics, provides a concrete theoretical pathway for engineering topological quantum states in solid-state systems.

The horizontal dashed lines de- note the corresponding theoretical predictions, α = −π/2 and α = −2π/3, respectively.

FIG. 2. Fusion channel selection. The electron density on the sphere for the MR state with 60 electrons and 4 quasi- holes, 2 at the north pole and the other 2 located at the same latitude. The quasiholes at the north pole fuse and form a (a) 1-anyon or (b) ψ-anyon.

FIG. 3. Numerical results for many-anyon braiding in the Moore–Read state. Panels (a) and (b) show the four- quasihole geometry and the resulting statistical Berry phase γstat, respectively. Panels (c) and (d) show the corresponding six-quasihole geometry and the relative eigenvalue phase α of the non-Abelian braiding matrix. The horizontal lines are the theoretical prediction in the two limits shown in Eqs. (3) and (4). In both geometries, two quasiholes are fused at the north pole, while the remaining quasiholes are braided in the presence of pinning potentials of strength h. They share the same legend in panel (b).
